subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class TUI observe or mirror mode for activity from other channel sessions, and should it be read-only, interactive, or limited to explicitly selected sessions?
rationale: This crosses channel and session visibility boundaries, likely adds CLI/config surface, and changes privacy and message-delivery expectations; source inspection proves the gap but cannot choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Add read-only observe mode
options.body: Add an explicit default-off observer that displays authorized cross-channel activity without sending mirrored replies to other transports.

options.title: Add interactive mirror mode
options.body: Allow bidirectional visible mirroring between TUI and channels behind stronger opt-in, accepting higher delivery and privacy risk.

options.title: Limit to selected-session live updates
options.body: Keep core work to the focused `session.message` live-update path and leave broader monitoring to logs or later design.

recommendation.title: Add read-only observe mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit default-off observer that displays authorized cross-channel activity without sending mirrored replies to other transports.

likelyOwner.reason: They are carrying the closest related TUI live-session work and are the best visible owner for choosing the broader session-visibility boundary.
